question: Should OpenClaw publish an OpenAPI/Swagger contract for Gateway access, and should its scope be documented HTTP routes only or a broader Gateway protocol discovery story?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the schema scope defines a new supported API/discovery contract across security-sensitive Gateway HTTP routes, existing TypeBox protocol schemas, and client SDK direction.

options.title: Approve scoped HTTP OpenAPI
options.body: Generate a versioned OpenAPI document for approved Gateway HTTP routes, document bearer/operator auth semantics, and keep WebSocket RPC on TypeBox/JSON Schema.

options.title: Defer to protocol docs
options.body: Keep Gateway protocol docs, RPC reference, and TypeBox/JSON Schema as the supported programmatic path until maintainers want an HTTP OpenAPI contract.

options.title: Serve runtime Swagger
options.body: Expose /openapi.json or Swagger UI from the Gateway only after approving route inclusion, auth requirements, and private-ingress behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped HTTP OpenAPI
recommendation.body: Generate a versioned OpenAPI document for approved Gateway HTTP routes, document bearer/operator auth semantics, and keep WebSocket RPC on TypeBox/JSON Schema.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across Gateway client/protocol packaging and public Gateway docs, which makes him the best available owner for the schema-scope decision.
